chapter_theme: A song at Thiruvarathurai (திருவரத்துறை): the poet asks whether he should fall to young women who flirt, steal hearts and wealth and exhaust a man on the bed; the praise makes Murugan the four-Veda child of Sirkazhi to whom the Lord of the shrine gave the pearl palanquin.

758.reading: The poet describes women who, angry or kind, put on kohl, call sweetly, recite poems, laugh and sport, melt the heart with arts of stealth, cruelly snatch away what a man had saved, embrace his neck and leave him faint on the bed, and asks whether he should be caught by them. The praise names Murugan as the one who stills birth, the partless Brahman in whose sea of conscious bliss sages bathe, and as the four-Veda child of Kochai to whom the Lord gave the pearl umbrella and palanquin, at Thiruvarathurai.
758.nuance: களவு வித்தை and முன் கருதி வைத்த வைப்பவை சேர தறுகணில் பறித்து: theft is named twice, of the heart and of the hoard. கொச்சை is Sirkazhi, and the pearl palanquin at Arathurai belongs to Sambandar's story; the song addresses that child as Murugan (சதுர்வேதச் சிறுவ), the book's identification of Murugan with Sambandar.
